newsitem.title: USA: Foxmeyer to exercise option on Hamilton.
newsitem.headline: Foxmeyer to exercise option on Hamilton.

text.p: Foxmeyer Health Corp said Thursday it would exercise its option to either sell its 69.8 percent majority investment in Hamilton Morgan LLC or buy the minority interest from the partnership's other major investor, Robert Haft.
Haft is chairman of Phar-Mor Inc.
Hamilton Morgan is a limited liability company whose sole investment is its about 31 percent stake, or 3.75 million shares, in Phar-Mor, a discount drug store chain.
FoxMeyer said its decision to implement the dispute-resolution process is based on dissatisfaction with its joint ownership of Hamilton Morgan.

On October 11, Phar-Mor said it and ShopKo Stores Inc had filed materials with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission outlining a proposed business combination in which shares of a newly formed holding company, Cabot Noble Inc, would be exchanged for shares of both Phar-Mor and ShopKo.
Phar-Mor said Thursday it was unable to determine what effect, if any, Foxmeyer's action on Hamilton would have on this proposed business combination.
Under the Hamilton agreement, Haft has 90 days to respond to FoxMeyer by agreeing either to sell his interest in Hamilton or buy FoxMeyer's interest, FoxMeyer said.
According to a FoxMeyer letter to Haft, a decision to buy FoxMeyer's interest would result in total cash proceeds of $26.6 million to FoxMeyer, or $9 per share, the company said.
If Haft elects to sell his shares, he would receive proceeds of about $7.2 million, the company said.
FoxMeyer said it also owned, and would still own after resolution of the Hamilton matter, one million Phar-Mor shares.
